name: Processor D (3x3 grid - team design)
source: Team-designed Phase 1 Processor D: 9-qubit 2D nearest-neighbour planar grid
design_rationale: Processor A (2016-inspired 5-qubit reference) has diameter 3 but exhibits multi-hop routing bottlenecks for peripheral leaf nodes (0, 3, 4). Processor B (9-qubit chorded mesh-loop) has diameter 4 and 12 edges, but features an asymmetric degree-5 hub (node 6) and a single-edge dead-end leaf (node 7), introducing physical frequency-crowding risks on node 6 and higher SWAP overhead (12 SWAPs) for distributed workloads like all-to-all entanglement. In contrast, Processor D employs a symmetric 3x3 planar grid (9 qubits, 12 bidirectional edges, diameter 4) that bounds maximum physical degree to 4, eliminates dead-end leaves (minimum degree 2), provides uniform multi-path alternative shortest paths, and achieves the lowest routing overhead (8 SWAPs vs 12 on B, a 33.3% reduction) for all-to-all workloads while remaining strictly 2D planar without wire crossovers.
note: Processor D is a team-designed supplemental topology for comparative analysis. Graph metrics: 9 qubits, 12 edges, diameter 4, avg_shortest_path 2.0, avg_swap_lower_bound 1.0, max_swap 3.
